meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: They have to be washed carefully by hand.
Put the glasses carefully on the table.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

examples.trans: The door is behind the wardrobe.

examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'corridor, hall' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: As you can see, a big hall.
He is standing in the corridor.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Short for может быть. Core Russian part meaning 'maybe, perhaps' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Мой муж = my husband. Common masculine noun meaning 'husband' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Nina, pour your husband a drink. We've got something to celebrate!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to visit'.

examples.text: Ваш муж хочет навестить вас после ужина.
examples.trans: Your husband wants to visit you after dinner.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и навестить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to visit on time.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: He left for a short time.

examples.text: Спасибо, я словно ненадолго вернулся домой!
examples.trans: Thank you, I felt as if I briefly returned home!

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.en: to answer, to reply, to pick up the phone
meanings.note: Отвечать кому / на звонок. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to answer, to reply', paired with 'ответить'.

examples.text: Я вам звоню, а вы не отвечаете!
examples.trans: I call you, and you don't answer!

examples.text: Почему ты не отвечаешь на мои вопросы?
examples.trans: Why aren't you answering my questions?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (root 'лучиться'). Used in Russian as a perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to more'.

examples.text: Лена, извини, мне нужно ещё раз отлучиться.
examples.trans: Lena, excuse me, I need to step away one more time.

examples.text: Что-то я тебя сегодня совсем не узнаю, Витя.
examples.trans: Somehow I do not recognize you at all today, Vitya.

meanings.en: to steam oneself (and beat with birch branches) in a Russian bathhouse
meanings.note: Не парься = don't sweat it. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to steam oneself in a bathhouse; (slang) to sweat over', paired with 'попариться'.

Не парься = don't sweat it. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to steam oneself in a bathhouse; (slang) to sweat over', paired with 'попариться'.

examples.text: В субботу мы паримся в бане.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: On foot. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Preposition + genitive, or adverb. Core Russian prep meaning 'after' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to check, to test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood. Check the soldering iron.

проводить.gloss: to see off, to see out

meanings.en: to see someone out, to see off
meanings.note: accompany someone to the door or the station
a different, imperfective verb проводить means 'to conduct, to spend (time)'

examples.text: Держи свои духи. Давай я тебя провожу. Пока!
examples.trans: Here is your perfume. Let me walk you out. Bye!

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

meanings.note: 'Проходите!' = Come in! (inviting a guest)

Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go through; to come in', paired with 'пройти'.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.

meanings.note: Building for goods storage. Common masculine noun meaning 'warehouse, storage' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хорошо, тогда встретимся на этом складе.
examples.trans: Fine, then we will meet at this warehouse.

examples.text: Ищи на складе и быстрее крутись!
examples.trans: Search in the storage and hustle faster!

meanings.note: Used as imperative exhortation.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: The room or the bowl. Common masculine noun meaning 'toilet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The toilet is in the corridor.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to see, to catch sight of
meanings.note: Вот увидишь! = you'll see!. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'видеть'.

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner, supper (evening meal)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

meanings.note: Целый день = all day long. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('whole, entire').
